diagnostic_evidence.quote: When $r = n_{\rm codim}^f +1 = \max\{m_i,m_j\}$, the linear space $\operatorname{colspan}(\mathbf{\bT}^{(f)})$ has complementary dimension to $X$, so by Bézout’s theorem~\cite[Theorem 18.3]{harris2013algebraic} the intersection consists of exactly $\deg X=r$ points.

issues.failure_explanation: The '+1' case of the formula is exactly the case deg X = n_codim^f + 1, i.e. X of minimal degree: then the span of r = n_codim^f + 1 generic rank-one factors is a general complementary-dimension linear space and, by the proof's own Bezout argument, meets X in exactly deg X = r points, so uniqueness holds at r = n_codim^f + 1. Minimal-degree Segre-Veronese varieties are not exhausted by 'two entries equal to 1 with min{m_i,m_j}=2' (Segre P^1 x P^{m_j-1}): they also include rational normal curves (single block f=(f_1), m_1=2: deg = f_1 = n_codim^f+1), the Veronese surface (f=(2), m_1=3: deg 4 = n_codim^f+1), and scrolls nu_{(s,1)}(P^1 x P^{k-1}) (f=(s,1), m_1=2: deg sk = n_codim^f+1). In those cases the 'otherwise' value is not the largest r: e.g. a generic rank-4 tensor T in S^4(R^3) with f=(2) (n_row=n_col=6, n_codim^f=3) has colspan(T^{(2)}) meeting the Veronese surface in exactly the 4 given points, so T^{(f)} has a unique rank-4 decomposition and r(f)=4, while the theorem states r(f)=min{6,3}=3. The proof's assertion 'deg X > r for all other tuples f' is false in these cases (deg X = r = 4), so the cited real-points non-uniqueness result is invoked outside its needed hypothesis.

failure_location.quote: For all other tuples $f$, we have $\deg X>r$ and there exist linear space of projective dimension $r-1$ that intersects $X$ in more than $r$ real points, see~\cite[Theorem 1.6]{ranestad2024real}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the case condition as 'deg X = n_codim^f + 1' (X of minimal degree: rational normal curves/scrolls, the Veronese surface, and the listed Segre case), which the existing Bezout argument already proves, and keep the 'otherwise' branch for deg X > n_codim^f + 1.
issues.overall_effect: The exact formula for the maximal recoverable rank r(f) - a main result underlying the flattening choice - under-reports r(f) by one in all minimal-degree cases not listed; the non-uniqueness claim at r = n_codim^f+1 is unsupported (and false over C) there. The specific values computed in cor:added-1 and the experiments happen to coincide with the corrected formula, so no downstream numeric result changes.
issues.title: Formula for r(f) misses minimal-degree (Bezout-tight) Segre-Veronese cases
issues.why_classification: The statement and case split of a main theorem must be corrected using the (known) classification of minimal-degree Segre-Veronese varieties: a contained, nontrivial revision of the same proof architecture (trisecant lemma + Bezout), with no change to the paper's computed ranks or conclusions.

issues.failure_explanation: h is decreasing on [0,1] (with h(1)=0). The proof's pointwise Hessian lower bound is -sqrt((f_i-1)/f_i) h(F_A(v)) + gamma_i, which is nonnegative only where h(F_A(v)) <= h(nu), i.e. where F_A(v) >= nu. Under the stated condition F <= nu one has h(F) >= h(nu), so the final estimate does not follow. Read literally, nu = 1 is admissible (F_A takes values in [0,1]) and prescribes gamma_i = h(1) = 0, i.e. no shift; but at tuples with small F_A the block Hessian of F_A is indefinite, so the block-convexity hypothesis of Theorem thm:power_method_convergence fails and global convergence is not guaranteed. The needed condition is a lower bound on F_A along the trajectory (e.g. the initial value, since PS-HOPM increases F).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'F <= nu' by the requirement that nu lower-bound F_A at the initialization (all visited points then satisfy F_A >= nu by monotone increase), and note that Theorem thm:power_method_convergence's ascent argument only uses block convexity at visited points.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised small (<1) shifts for PS-HOPM on the symmetrized tensor Ttilde^{(f)} are unjustified as stated; for the admissible choice nu = 1 the proposition prescribes zero shift, for which the global-convergence guarantee of Theorem thm:power_method_convergence does not apply.
issues.title: Shift prescription uses the wrong inequality direction (F <= nu instead of a lower bound)
issues.why_classification: The correction changes the meaning of the hypothesis (shift tied to initialization) and requires a short superlevel-set convexity argument; a comparable speedup result survives, but as written the proposition supports invalid shift choices (e.g. nu = 1), so the guarantee is lost without the fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The matrix $(J\Psi_1)_{1,1}$ is symmetric and its eigenvalues are at least $0$  by \eqref{eq: J11} and $F_1$ being convex, and they are at most $1$ by \eqref{eq: J11 H11} and since $\mathbf{H}_{1,1}$ is negative definite, being a submatrix of the Hessian at a maximizer.

issues.failure_explanation: A second-order critical point only has negative SEMIdefinite Riemannian Hessian; the proof's claim that H_{1,1} 'is negative definite, being a submatrix of the Hessian at a maximizer' is unjustified. If the Hessian has a kernel, J Psi has eigenvalue 1: for v in ker H_{1,1}, semidefiniteness of the full Hessian forces H_{2,1}v = 0, so (v,0) is an eigenvector of J Psi with eigenvalue 1, and the spectral-radius argument fails. The conclusion is false as stated: take T in S^2(R^2) x S^4(R^2) with <T, v^{\otimes 2} x w^{\otimes 4}> = ||v||^4(w_1^2+w_2^2)^2 - 2||v||^4 w_2^4; on spheres F_0 = v_1^2(1-2w_2^4) <= 1 with pSVT singular values <= 1; with shifts gamma_1 = 1, gamma_2 = 5 the function F is convex in each block; the global maxima (any unit v, w = e_1) are degenerate second-order critical points with sigma = 1 > 0; the block-2 update near w_2 = t is t -> t - (2/(1+gamma_2)) t^3 + O(t^5), so convergence is algebraic (t_k ~ k^{-1/2}), not linear. Additionally, eq:lambda mu drops the factors ||v||^2, ||w||^2 from the eigen equations (lambda ||v||^2 = beta_1 + mu/alpha_1 etc.); the subsequent conclusions survive only after restoring them.

failure_location.quote: PS–HOPM on $\sT$ with shifts $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$ has local linear convergence around every pSVT that is a second-order critical point of $F$ with positive singular value on the product of spheres ${\SB^{m_1-1}\times \SB^{m_2-1}}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the statement to strict second-order critical points (negative definite Riemannian Hessian) and restore the norm factors in eq:lambda mu; then the eigenvalue analysis yields spectral radius < 1.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition's guarantee of local linear convergence is false for degenerate second-order critical points (which occur, e.g., for tensors with continuous families of maximizers); only strict (nondegenerate) second-order critical points are covered by a correct argument.
issues.title: Local linear convergence claimed at all second-order critical points, but fails at degenerate ones
issues.why_classification: The statement as written is false, not merely unproven; the repair is a limited weakening (strictness hypothesis) plus routine fixes to the displayed eigen equations, leaving a recognizably comparable local-convergence result for the generic (nondegenerate) case.

issues.failure_explanation: From <T_w, R^{(i)}> = mu_i + sum_{j != i} mu_j <R^{(j)}, R^{(i)}> one only obtains |mu_i - <R^{(i)}, T_w>| <= (r-1) rho ||mu||_infty, since the sum has r-1 terms each bounded by rho ||mu||_infty; the factor r-1 is dropped. Consequently ||mu||_infty <= max_i |<R^{(i)}, T_w>|/(1-rho) and the constant C = (1-rho)^{-1} (prod_k (1+(r-1) rho_k))^{1/l} are not established; the valid bound of this form has denominator 1-(r-1)rho and requires (r-1)rho < 1. The stated inequality is false in general: with l=2, f=(1,1), r=3, take R^{(i)} = a x b_i with b_1 = e_1, b_2 = 0.6 e_1 + 0.8 e_2, and b_3 a slight perturbation of 0.6 e_1 - 0.8 e_2 (rho = 0.6, nearly singular Gram matrix), w^{(1)} = a and w^{(2)} in span{b_i} along the bottom Gram eigenvector: then F_A = 1 but max_i |<R^{(i)}, T_w>| ~ 0.145 while C ~ 6.42, giving C max_i |<.>| ~ 0.93 < 1 = F_A.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace rho ||mu||_infty by (r-1) rho ||mu||_infty, yielding C = (1-(r-1)rho)^{-1}(prod_k(1+(r-1)rho_k))^{1/l}, and add the hypothesis (r-1)rho < 1.
issues.overall_effect: The upper bound in Theorem thm:added-2 (the paper's guarantee that critical points of F_A are either low-value or near a true component) is false as stated; a correct version needs the larger denominator 1-(r-1)rho and the extra hypothesis (r-1)rho < 1, materially changing the constant.
issues.title: Coherence bound in F_A estimate drops a factor (r-1); constant C is wrong
issues.why_classification: The proof's key estimate is wrong and the stated constant is not merely unproven but falsifiable; the repair is contained (corrected constant plus an added hypothesis) and leaves a comparable, though quantitatively weaker, bound.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
When all the rows of each $\bM_j$ are orthonormal, we have $\rho=\rho_1=\cdots=\rho_\ell=0$, and hence
\(
\max_i |\langle \sR^{(i)}, \mathscr{T}_\fw\rangle|^2
\;\le\; F_\Acal(\fw^{(1)},\ldots,\fw^{(\ell)})
\;\le\; \max_i |\langle \sR^{(i)}, \mathscr{T}_\fw\rangle|\).

issues.failure_explanation: The inequality |<.>|^{ell f_j} <= |<.>|^2 uses |<.>| <= 1 and hence requires ell f_j >= 2. For a block with f_j = 0 the left side of eq:gershgorin equals sum_i 1 = r, which is not <= sum_i <.>^2 (<= 1 + (r-1) rho_j); likewise for ell = f_j = 1. In those regimes - which include the paper's main flattening choices such as f = (1,1,0) - the stated upper bound is false: take ell = 2, f = (1,0), r = 2 with orthonormal v_1^{(1)}, v_2^{(1)} and orthonormal v_1^{(2)}, v_2^{(2)} (so rho = rho_1 = rho_2 = 0 and C = 1), A = span{v_1^{(1)}, v_2^{(1)}}, w^{(1)} = (v_1^{(1)}+v_2^{(1)})/sqrt(2): then F_A = 1 but C max_i |<R^{(i)}, T_w>| = 1/sqrt(2) < 1. The same counterexample violates the following remark's claim F_A <= max_i |<R^{(i)}, T_w>| in the orthonormal case. This defect is independent of the dropped (r-1) factor (ISSUE-004): it persists after that constant is corrected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the theorem to tuples with f_j >= 1 for all j (and ell f_j >= 2), or keep zero blocks at the price of an extra factor r^{z/ell} (z = number of zero blocks) in C; the remark likewise needs f_j >= 1.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's upper bound, and the simplifying remark after it, are false for flattening tuples with a zero block (the paper's principal use case) and for ell = f_j = 1; the proximity guarantee for critical points of F_A is lost in those regimes.
issues.title: Upper bound of Theorem thm:added-2 fails when some f_j = 0 (or ell = f_j = 1)
issues.why_classification: The statement is false within its advertised scope (concrete counterexample); the fix is a contained scope restriction or a corrected constant, leaving a comparable bound for all-positive tuples.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\Acal=\Span\Bigl\{\,\bigotimes_{j=1}^\ell (\fv_{i}^{(j)})^{\otimes d_j}\ :\ 1\leq i\leq r\,\Bigr\}$, where the vectors $\fv_{i}^{(j)}$ are generic with norm one, and assume $\dim \Acal = r$.

issues.failure_explanation: The statement assumes only genericity and dim A = r, but the uniqueness conclusion is proved via the claim that A contains no rank-one tensors other than the r summands R^{(i)}_{(d)} - a trisecant-type condition that the proof imports through 'since r <= r(f)', a hypothesis appearing nowhere in the statement (only in the section's prose). Without such a hypothesis the conclusion fails: if r is large (e.g. A a hyperplane), the space {u : u x R^{(i)}_{(f)} in A} is a hyperplane in the multidegree-(d-f) space and contains many rank-one tensors, so Vect(R^{(i)}_{(d-f)}) is not the unique rank-one left singular vector with singular value one. Additionally, the quoted sentence is garbled: the R^{(i)}_{(f)} do not lie in A (a subspace of the multidegree-d space); the claim should concern the R^{(i)}_{(d)}.

failure_location.quote: Moreover, the $r$ rank-one tensors $\{\mathscr{R}^{(i)}_{(f)}\}_{i=1}^r$ are the only rank-one elements in $\Acal$ (up to scale), since $r \leq r(f)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis r <= r(f) (or, equivalently, that the only rank-one tensors in A are the r summands) to the statement and correct the claim to concern R^{(i)}_{(d)}.
issues.overall_effect: As a standalone statement the theorem is false; its validity is limited to the regime r <= r(f) (which implies the needed uniqueness of rank-one elements of A), as assumed in the surrounding section and used by cor: r_max with matching and Algorithm alg: recover complement.
issues.title: Theorem thm: match up patterns omits the rank hypothesis its proof relies on
issues.why_classification: The missing condition is exactly the standing assumption of the section and the regime of all applications; importing it into the statement and fixing the index of the rank-one tensors is a local repair that preserves the result and its uses.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For unique decomposition of $\sT$, the largest rank $r$ need to satisfy $r\leq r(g)$ for any flattening tuple $g$ used either to extract rank-one tensors via pSVTs as in Theorem \ref{thm:decomp and singular vector} or to recover complementary factors as in Algorithm \ref{alg: recover complement}.

issues.failure_explanation: For a symmetry-breaking flattening, the complement is recovered from the SAME f-flattening (Theorem thm: match up patterns and the symmetry-breaking branch of Algorithm alg: recover complement use only the row span of T^{(f)}); the uniqueness needed there is that A contain no rank-one tensors besides the r summands, which follows from r <= r(f) (since r(f) <= n_codim^f + 1 <= n_codim^d). No r(d-f) condition arises, so the largest recoverable rank is r(f), not min{r(f), r(d-f)}. The displayed formula is wrong: e.g. d=(5,1), f=(4,0), m_1=3, m_2=5 gives r(f)=12 but r(d-f)=r((1,1))=8, so the corollary caps the recoverable rank at 8 while extraction at rank 12 plus Theorem thm: match up patterns completion works; worse, d=(4,1), f=(3,0) gives r(d-f)=r((1,1)) which can fall below r(f). The second equality additionally ignores both the n_col cap and the '+1' special case of Theorem thm:rmax_formula: d=(2,2), f=(1,1), m_1=2, m_2=3 gives min{r(f),r(d-f)} = 3 but min{n_codim^f, n_codim^{d-f}} = 2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Item 2 should read r_max(f) = r(f) (justified by Theorem thm: match up patterns under r <= r(f)); delete the incorrect evaluated equality or restore the min with n_col and the case distinction.
issues.overall_effect: The stated maximal recoverable rank for symmetry-breaking flattenings is under-reported (in some cases drastically), and the corollary is internally inconsistent with Theorem thm: match up patterns and with the candidate values r((k,1)) used in cor:added-1; the second equality is false whenever the special case of Theorem thm:rmax_formula applies or n_col binds.
issues.title: Corollary cor: r_max with matching, item 2: spurious r(d-f) condition and false evaluated equality
issues.why_classification: A displayed summary formula for the achievable rank is wrong and contradicts the paper's own completion theorem; the repair is contained (drop the spurious condition), but it changes the stated values and requires re-justification via the trisecant condition, so it is more than a local typo fix.

issues.failure_explanation: For ell = 4, d=(4,1), f=(1,1), Theorem thm:rmax_formula's two-ones special case applies whenever min{n,k}=2, giving r(1,1) = min{ binom(n+2,3), (n-1)(k-1)+1 }. Hence for k=2 the correct value is min{ binom(n+2,3), n } = n, not min{4,n} as displayed (wrong for n >= 5), and for n=2 it is min{4,k}, so r(1,1) = 4 > 3 = r(2,1) once k >= 4, contradicting 'When n=2 ... (2,1) dominates'. Consequently the stated optimal-tuple threshold is wrong at (n,k) = (2,4): the corollary selects (2,1) (value 3) while (1,1) achieves 4. The general threshold (n^2+3n-2)/(2n-2) is derived under n>2, k>2 and is correct there.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the special-case values (r(1,1) = min{ binom(n+2,3), n } for k=2 and min{4,k} for n=2) and treat n=2 separately, e.g. (1,1) optimal for k >= 3 (tie at k=3) and (2,1) for k=2 when n=2.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary's optimal-flattening prescription is false in the corner case n=2, 3 <= k <= 4 (at k=4 it names a strictly suboptimal tuple), and the displayed r(1,1) values for k=2 are wrong for n >= 5; all conclusions for n > 2 survive.
issues.title: Corollary cor:added-1 mishandles the n=2 / k=2 cases; threshold wrong at (n,k)=(2,4)
issues.why_classification: Only the n=2 corner and a secondary displayed value are affected; the main threshold for n>2 and the qualitative conclusions survive, and the repair is a short recomputation in degenerate cases.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we introduce a new tensor $\widetilde{\sT}^{(f)}$ such that the pSVTs of $\sT^{(f)}$ and $\widetilde{\sT}^{(f)}$ are in one-to-one correspondence.

issues.failure_explanation: The vector w is defined by rescaling T^{(f)} . otimes_i (v^{(i)})^{f_i} to unit norm, which is impossible when this contraction is zero. Any tuple with otimes_i (v^{(i)})^{f_i} orthogonal to A is a pSVT of Ttilde^{(f)} with singular value sigma^2 = 0 (every contraction vanishes because each term contains the factor <S_j, otimes_i (v^{(i)})^{f_i}> = 0), but it has no corresponding pSVT of T^{(f)}, so the 'if and only if' fails at singular value zero and the proof only establishes the correspondence for sigma > 0. The Section 5 prose claim that the pSVTs of the two tensors 'are in one-to-one correspondence' inherits the same inaccuracy.

failure_location.quote:
is a pSVT of $\widetilde{\sT}^{(f)}$ with singular value $\sigma^2$ if and only if $(\fv^{(1)},\ldots,\fv^{(\ell)},\fw)$ is a pSVT of $\sT^{(f)}$ with singular value $\sigma$, where
    \(
    \fw \) is the vector \( \sT^{(f)} \cdot \bigotimes_{i=1}^\ell {(\fv^{(i)})}^{\otimes f_i} \), rescaled to be norm one.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict part (1) to nonzero singular values (equivalently, tuples with T^{(f)} . otimes_i (v^{(i)})^{f_i} != 0) and adjust the one-to-one correspondence prose accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The stated bijection is false in the degenerate zero-singular-value case; all uses of the lemma concern singular value one (or the identity F_A = <Ttilde^{(f)}, otimes (v^{(i)})^{2f_i}> in part (2)), which are unaffected.
issues.title: pSVT correspondence between Ttilde^{(f)} and T^{(f)} fails at singular value zero
issues.why_classification: A local degenerate-case fix: the correspondence and every downstream use (singular value one) survive unchanged; no nontrivial new argument is needed.
